topic: Distal radius fracture time to surgery
usual_baseline: Extra-articular fractures mostly meet the 7-day target (82–100%). Intra-articular fractures within 72 hours range from 4.3% to 65%. Hand trauma audits in this group show 46–86% within BSSH timeframes. Theatre capacity is the usual cause of delay: 73.7% of delays in one audit [1721] and 52% in another [1707].
fix_that_works: Hand trauma timeliness met the project target, overall compliance 73% to 83%, bites 100% [1707]. Referral-based intra-articular timing rose 74% to 88% after education and a trauma list dropdown [1716].
fix_that_fails: Education and a dropdown did not hold: intra-articular within 3 days of injury 59% to 75% then 56%, extra-articular fell to 68% [1716]. Registrar email, teaching and a pathway left intra-articular compliance at 10% [1721]. Theatre efficiency recommendations: 74% to 72% [2494]. Flexor tendon surgery stayed at 86% [2182].
consultant_advice: Teaching does not fix a theatre capacity problem, and these audits show it. Audit the pathway steps instead, with timestamps from injury to listing to surgery. The virtual fracture clinic route (0% compliant vs 37.5%) [1752] is the most useful thing to measure.
